propositions: Commit bodies on main are inconsistently wrapped (5 of 40 recent commits conform; 35 fail with lines ranging 129-286 characters) due to lack of local enforcement.

A commit-msg hook must reject commits with subjects exceeding 50 characters or body lines exceeding 72 characters, while preserving Gerrit's Change-Id stamping by chaining rather than clobbering the existing hook.
The checker must exempt trailers, TAG= lines, fenced code blocks, indented literal blocks, table rows, and lines whose length comes from unsplittable atomic tokens (URLs, paths, dotted identifiers).
The enforcement is local and operator-driven via pre-commit framework at the commit-msg stage, with no CI check and bypass possible via --no-verify.
The hook must not mutate commit messages and git scaffolding (comments, --verbose diff) must not trigger false positives.
